A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including Appendices A–C in v1 and A–D in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original forecasting comparisons, timing measurements, and ablations on Burgers’, Shallow Water, and Navier–Stokes datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds Scalar Flow results, latent-dimension experiments, and the dynamics/decoder-capacity study in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The generative model, transformer architecture, latent ODE, interpolation, and ELBO are retained. However, v2 Sections 4.2–4.3 specify all N observations as encoder input, whereas v1 specifies Nctx context observations; v2 Appendix B still specifies Nctx. This inconsistency prevents determining whether training inputs actually changed or only their presentation changed.

E1.justification: v2 adds Scalar Flow, extending evaluation from three simulated PDE systems to measured smoke-plume videos. Appendix A.4 constructs density-dependent observations from camera images without the explicit Poisson sampling used for the synthetic datasets. This adds materially different data and observation conditions.

E2.justification: Table 3 and Appendix C.4 retain the same comparators: median prediction, FEN, NSPDE, CNN-ODE, constant intensity, DSTPP, NSTPP, and AutoSTPP. Their extension to Scalar Flow does not change comparator membership; publication-year updates also do not identify different methods.

E3.justification: v2 introduces Scalar Flow preprocessing and sampling, an 80/10/10 trajectory split, and a 1.25-second context, plus latent-dimension and dynamics/decoder-width sweeps. Section 5 also changes the stated half-context range from Nctx/2 through 1 to Nctx/2 through Nctx, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing synthetic splits, metrics, training budgets, and solver settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 tests whether low-dimensional latent states suffice. Appendix D and Table 4 investigate whether decoder capacity compensates for simpler dynamics by varying latent dimension and both network widths. Existing context-size, interpolation, and observation/process-removal analyses are also extended to Scalar Flow.

E5.justification: Both Table 3 captions specify one standard error over five random seeds controlling model initialization. v2 extends this practice to additional results without changing the stated repetition count or introducing confidence intervals, significance tests, or another uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: The synthetic values in Tables 1–3 are retained, while v2 adds Scalar Flow results, Figure 6 curves, and Table 4 capacity results. On Scalar Flow, Table 3 reports MAE 0.092 ± 0.002 for the proposed method versus CNN-ODE’s 0.091 ± 0.001, and log-likelihood 8.41 ± 0.04 versus AutoSTPP’s 8.49 ± 0.05. These are new benchmark findings, not improvements under the original settings.

T1.justification: Equation 13 changes the formal KL target from a posterior conditioned on Nctx observations to one conditioned on N observations, matching the scope of the retained ELBO. Section 4.4 additionally writes out posterior-predictive integrals. The generative assumptions and Appendix B derivation otherwise remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain joint modeling of dynamics and observation events, efficient interpolation-based latent-state evaluation, and strong benchmark performance. The marked-point-process framing and conclusion’s statement about low-resolution linear interpolation restate the existing setup and v1’s Figure 5 finding rather than introduce a different core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix D adds a substantive explanation of how decoder capacity can reduce the benefit of complex latent dynamics. Section 5 qualifies baseline superiority on Scalar Flow and suggests its context benefits may not have saturated. The relocated limitations paragraph retains the original restrictions but adds the need for sufficiently dense sensor placement to capture event intensity.

D1.justification: The first-page footnote replaces a promised release with a repository link for code and datasets. Appendix A.4 documents Scalar Flow resolution, smoothing, sampling probability, and splits; Appendix D specifies capacity-study configurations, and Section 4.4 explains predictive averaging. Existing implementation details largely persist, although the timing experiment’s explicit n = 20 qualifier is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Scalar Flow reference, Eckert et al. (2019), and explicitly contrasts its generative variational approach with discriminative encode-process-decode models. Most other reference changes update publication metadata for works already cited.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, edits the abstract and introduction, rewrites the inference and encoder explanations, adds a dedicated forecasting subsection, and moves limitations from Section 3 to the conclusion. The overall section sequence and most existing prose remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The empirical displays are substantially expanded: Figure 3 gains a smoke-video row, Figures 4–5 gain Scalar Flow curves and secondary axes, Tables 1–3 gain dataset entries, and Figure 6 and Table 4 are new. The model diagram is lightly redrawn and the document adopts ICLR formatting. Appendix trajectory histograms are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens two weaknesses of v1: evaluation confined to simulated systems and limited investigation of why simple latent trajectories work well. Scalar Flow supplies measured dynamics with an emulated observation process, while Appendix D tests the decoder-capacity explanation and qualifies the need for complex dynamics. Explicit forecasting documentation and reported code/data access also help. The gains concern validation and understanding: Scalar Flow does not establish superiority over the strongest baselines, and the inconsistent encoder-input descriptions remain a reproducibility limitation.
